finding.claim: LFS upload and verify URLs are taken from the LFS server's batch response and passed to urllib.request.urlopen with no scheme or host check, bypassing the configured urllib3 pool manager. A hostile or MITM'd LFS endpoint can redirect the PUT body (the object being pushed) and server-chosen headers to any host the client can reach (SSRF). Medium-low severity: the body is data already being sent to that endpoint, so the main impact is cross-host redirection and internal network reach, not new data exposure.
finding.source: LFS batch JSON response: actions.upload.href, actions.upload.header, actions.verify.href (attacker-controlled by the LFS server)
finding.sink: urlopen(Request(upload_url, data=content, method="PUT")) at lfs.py:757 and urlopen(Request(verify_action.href, data=..., method="POST")) at lfs.py:772

trace.note: batch response parsed; href = action_data["href"] taken verbatim from server JSON
upload_action = obj.actions["upload"]; only checks that the 'upload' key exists
upload_url = upload_action.href (no validation)
Request(upload_url, data=content, method="PUT") - content is the user's object bytes
server-supplied header map copied onto the request
urlopen(req) - accepts http, https, and file URLs; no scheme/host allowlist, no origin check
verify href used unvalidated for a POST with JSON {oid,size}
urlopen(req) for verify

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist exists only for the configured base LFS URL (lfs.py:380-393, 464-470, 519), not for server-returned hrefs. The download path (lfs.py:697-705) uses the configured urllib3 pool manager and never calls urlopen, so the upload path is inconsistent with it. file:// PUT/POST bodies are ignored by urllib and no response body is returned, so local file exfiltration via this path was not demonstrated. Precondition: the user pushes LFS content to an attacker-controlled or MITM'd LFS endpoint.

finding.claim: The public default for build_index_from_tree's validate_path_element is validate_path_element_default, which only rejects .git, ., .., and empty names (case-insensitively). Library callers that rely on the default can materialize NTFS-aliased .git spellings such as git~1, .git., or .git  (trailing dot/space, or 8.3 short name) on Windows, which resolve to the repository's .git directory. Writing hooks/post-checkout there gives code execution on the next git command. Low severity: every in-repo caller passes a config-derived validator, so this needs a direct library call with the default on Windows.
finding.source: Tree entry names in a malicious repository, supplied to a direct caller of build_index_from_tree with no validate_path_element argument
finding.sink: build_file_from_blob writes the blob to root/<entry path> via open(target_path, "wb") at index.py:1916 after build_index_from_tree at index.py:2227-2253

validate_path_element_default only checks _normalize_path_element_default(element) not in INVALID_DOTNAMES
_normalize_path_element_default is element.lower(); no NTFS 8.3, trailing-dot, or trailing-space handling
validate_path(entry.path, validate_path_element) with the weak default
full_path = _tree_to_fs_path(root_path, entry.path, ...)
build_file_from_blob writes the blob under the path
open(target_path, "wb") writes to the aliased .git path on Windows

finding.guards_checked: The stronger validators exist and are used by all in-repo callers: _is_ntfs_dotgit (index.py:2031-2075) and validate_path_element_ntfs (index.py:2078), selected by get_path_element_validator with core.protectNTFS default true (index.py:2163-2168). porcelain/__init__.py:6239, porcelain/submodule.py:259, and worktree.py:847 all pass the config-derived validator. The leaf-symlink check in build_file_from_blob (index.py:1893-1910) is unrelated to this name-aliasing issue. Not exploitable via normal porcelain clone or checkout; it needs a direct library call with the default on Windows.

finding.claim: The LFS test server accepts unauthenticated uploads and reads the entire request body into memory with no size cap, in both handle_upload and handle_verify. A remote client can exhaust memory or disk with large bodies (OIDs are checked against SHA-256 of the body, so the client must supply content that hashes to its chosen oid, but any size is allowed). Low severity: the module is documented as a test server, and the default bind is localhost.
finding.source: HTTP PUT /objects/<oid> body and Content-Length, and POST /objects/<oid>/verify Content-Length (any unauthenticated client)
finding.sink: chunks list accumulated in handle_upload (lfs_server.py:205-216) then lfs_store.write_object(chunks) (lfs_server.py:227); handle_verify reads Content-Length bytes with rfile.read (lfs_server.py:246-249)

remaining = content_length, loop reads until exhausted, appending to chunks

_object_exists check, then write_object(chunks) to disk (lfs.py:177-179 writes tmp file)
handle_verify: content_length from header, no cap
self.rfile.read(content_length) reads full body into memory

finding.guards_checked: _is_valid_oid enforces 64 lowercase hex characters (lfs_server.py:42-48, 198, 242), blocking path traversal through the oid. The SHA-256 match is enforced (217-222), so only content that hashes to the requested oid is stored. Client-supplied Host header is reflected into batch hrefs (lfs_server.py:143, 152, 156); this only affects the same client's response and was not treated as a separate finding.
